correctness.rationale: The gauge φ=e^{-vx/(2D)}u turns the backward drift operator into a real self-adjoint Robin form with h=v/(2D). An exact completion of two squares proves E[u]≥v||u||∞². Compactness and equality in those squares give unique critical measure vδ_a. A positive piecewise exponential eigenfunction proves λ(vδ_a)=0 with the exact jump and Robin boundaries. The variational form gives λ signs for β≠v. For β>v the jump equation β/D=g_q(a)+g_q(L-a), strict Riccati concavity in t and monotonicity in q give reflection symmetry and strict center minimum. The uniform-vs-delta witness follows from E[u]≥v²/(4D)||u||² and the delta threshold. The standalone checker redoes exact piecewise-linear identities and numeric test cases; infinite quantifiers are covered by the written proof, not numerical experiments.

originality.rationale: The tested scientific claim is the sharp universal total-growth barrier B=v, its unique atomic equality case, the strict supercritical center penalty, and the same-budget opposite-sign construction for a fixed Neumann/Robin backward drift operator. The initiating paper derives the spectral framework but limits its growth profile to self-consistent bacterial division and step-function approximations. The most relevant accessible optimization paper analyzes a mathematically different drift and bounded sign-indefinite resources. Classical Robin point-potential and rearrangement tools are not claimed as novel. Targeted published-finding searches and broader primary literature comparisons revealed no matching stronger implication, subject to stated priority risks.
residual_risks: The exact sharp trace inequality or a general one-dimensional delta-potential optimization theorem may already be contained in older mathematical physics or Sturm–Liouville literature; not all such full texts were inspected.
The growth measure is an independent idealization, not a self-consistent birth-rate field derived in the biological paper.
The 2008 review and some old general point-interaction literature were not exhaustively inspected; publication priority remains literature-bounded.

value.rationale: The question asks for the minimal integrated reproductive resource that can overcome outflow in a one-dimensional bacterial branching environment. The result gives the universal sharp lower budget v independent of diffusivity, length and position, shows only atomic concentration saturates that bound, and classifies the hotspot-position penalty beyond it. The same-budget explicit case proves a distributed resource can fail while an equally costly concentrated source succeeds. This distinguishes establishment budget from local reproduction intensity and provides a new exact benchmark for flow-structured ecological spectral models, even without any general nonlinear theorem.
